name: Monarchism
summary: Monarchism advocates monarchy, usually hereditary, as the best head of state or form of government. Its defenders argue that a crown gives continuity, national unity and a non-partisan office above party strife, and some hold it restrains demagogues and mob rule. Most living adherents back constitutional monarchy, while Legitimist and absolutist strands defend hereditary right, religion and a stronger crown.
scope: Mainstream modern monarchism as the advocacy of the institution (distinct from royalism for a particular monarch), centred on constitutional monarchy as described by Bogdanor and Otto von Habsburg, with Hobbes's Leviathan as the main primary text on monarchy's advantages and French Legitimism as the traditionalist strand. It excludes particular dynastic claims, and the economic and cultural views of individual parties are treated as unaddressed.

keyFigures.name: Thomas Hobbes
keyFigures.role: Philosopher whose Leviathan argues monarchy is the best form of sovereignty.

keyFigures.name: Joseph de Maistre
keyFigures.role: Counter-revolutionary philosopher of monarchy, author of Considerations on France.

keyFigures.name: Otto von Habsburg
keyFigures.role: Heir to the Austro-Hungarian crown who advocated constitutional hereditary monarchy.

sources.title: Monarchism
sources.author: Wikipedia

sources.title: Leviathan, chapter 19
sources.author: Thomas Hobbes
sources.usedFor: Argument that a monarch's private interest matches the public one, indivisible sovereignty and succession.

sources.author: Wikipedia

sources.title: Legitimists
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Hereditary legitimacy, Catholic kingship, tradition and counter-revolution.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Monarchism as such has no health policy; constitutional monarchies span the Nordic welfare states to Gulf rentier states, so adherents split by wider party loyalty.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The ideology is silent on wage law; monarchists in Britain, Spain and Japan take whatever economic line their party does.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Economic doctrine is not part of monarchism; Hoppe is pro-market while Catholic and Tory monarchists are paternalist, so the camp is split.

public-ownership.rationale: Inferred: conservative monarchist tradition leans toward existing property arrangements, but crown-owned estates and royal monopolies show no firm doctrine.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred: hereditary-rank, landed-wealth sympathies tilt monarchists against heavy wealth taxes, though the sources state no tax position.

unions-good.rationale: No stated position; Legitimists favoured corporate bodies and guilds in principle, but the modern movement has no union stance.

property-fundamental.rationale: Inferred: hereditary succession itself rests on inherited title and property, so adherents usually value strong property rights, though Hobbes lets the sovereign override them.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Not an issue the monarchist tradition addresses; adherents split along party lines.

cut-welfare.rationale: No doctrine; Ultra-royalist paternalism and Hoppe's libertarianism point in opposite directions.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred: hierarchical, tradition-based monarchism does not favour worker-owned firms, though it does not oppose them explicitly.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Hobbes prizes security above liberty, but constitutional monarchists defend civil liberties against mob and tyrant alike; no settled view.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the socially conservative and religious leaning of most monarchist movements.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: No stated position; monarchist liberty arguments (Kuehnelt-Leddihn) cut against speech codes while order-minded adherents accept them.

strong-leader.rationale: Constitutional monarchists value monarchy as a check that keeps populist strongmen out, though absolutist strands and Hobbes prefer unified power.

state-harmful.rationale: Monarchism upholds a state headed by a crown; Hobbes treats sovereignty as the artificial soul of the commonwealth, so anarchism is flatly rejected.

limit-guns.rationale: No doctrine; adherents differ by country, from British restriction to American-style gun rights.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred: order and loyalty to the crown, and the monarch's role as head of the armed forces, incline adherents to support security institutions.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the religious and traditionalist character of the Legitimist and Catholic monarchist currents.

decide-locally.rationale: Divided: Habsburg-style monarchists favour subsidiarity and regional crowns, while Hobbes holds sovereignty indivisible and Bogdanor sees the crown unifying multinational states.

rehabilitation.rationale: No stated position on penal philosophy; no settled monarchist view.

traditional-family.rationale: Dynastic succession makes the family central to the institution, and the Legitimist tradition is closely tied to Catholic family teaching.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Traditional monarchists generally oppose it, but many constitutional monarchists in Western Europe accept it, so this is contested.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred: Catholic and traditionalist monarchists oppose it, but constitutional monarchists in secular states often do not take a line.

more-religion-public.rationale: Monarchy is historically sacral: Japan's emperor heads Shinto, Bossuet derived kingship from scripture, and Legitimists demand a Catholic king.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not a monarchist concern; adherents divide by party and country.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred: traditionalist monarchism, with its hereditary and often male-preference succession, leans to natural differences.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Monarchy is defended as the embodiment of continuity and national tradition, and Legitimists base their case on inherited fundamental laws.

gradual-change.rationale: Monarchists prize continuity: the crown is defended as a stable keystone, and gradual evolution of custom is preferred to abrupt rupture.

reduce-immigration.rationale: No doctrine; the issue splits monarchists as it splits conservatives generally.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred: monarchy stands on national sovereignty and Hobbes's indivisible sovereign, so binding supranational power is generally resisted.

free-trade.rationale: No monarchist trade doctrine; both free-trade and protectionist monarchists have existed.

nation-first.rationale: Inferred: loyalty to a crown that embodies the nation inclines adherents to national interest, though Habsburg monarchism was supranational.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: No stated position; adherents split on foreign policy.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred: a monarchy is tied to a territory and people under a crown, and open borders are far from the tradition; no source states it.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed by monarchism; no consistent view.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: No doctrine; monarchs such as the UK's king speak for environmental concern, but adherents' policy views vary.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Inferred: the traditionalist and religious current doubts that technology can solve moral and political problems.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No doctrine and nothing in sources; split along ordinary party lines.

revolution-justified.rationale: Legitimists and Ultras were counter-revolutionary, and Maistre and Burke-style monarchism treat revolution as a catastrophe; only restorations against usurpers are defended.

experts-over-public.rationale: Hereditary monarchists reject expertise as a title to rule, but also distrust mass opinion; split.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred: Hobbes and traditional monarchism offer no case for planned economies and favour customary order.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred; no monarchist source discusses market socialism, and traditionalists lean against it.

land-value-tax.rationale: No position; a niche economic question outside monarchism.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred: hereditary succession rests on the principle of inheritance, so heavy taxation of it sits badly with adherents, though no source addresses taxes.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: No monarchist trade doctrine; mercantilist kings and free-trading constitutional monarchists both exist.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Absolutist kings ran mercantilist policy but modern constitutional monarchists defer to ministers; no settled view.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Not a monarchist doctrine, though Catholic and agrarian traditionalists sometimes favour it.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Inferred: monarchism upholds existing hierarchies and rejects utopian abolition schemes; no source addresses the question directly.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Hoppe's libertarian monarchism says yes, but mainstream monarchists have no view; genuinely split.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Legitimist and Catholic traditions favoured corporate bodies, but most modern monarchists have no stance.

one-party-rule.rationale: Monarchy is defended as a non-partisan office above party strife, and Legitimists and constitutional monarchists alike reject single-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: This is the defining claim of monarchism: advocacy of monarchy, hereditary in the usual form, as a good system of government.

democracy-best.rationale: Split: constitutional monarchists accept parliamentary democracy under the crown, while Hoppe, Kuehnelt-Leddihn and Legitimists distrust it.

direct-votes.rationale: Inferred: Hobbes, Legitimists and Kuehnelt-Leddihn (who warned of mob rule) distrust direct popular legislation.

workers-councils.rationale: Inferred: councils as the basis of power contradict the hierarchical, crown-centred order; no source addresses them.

right-to-secede.rationale: Inferred: sovereignty is indivisible in Hobbes and monarchs symbolise the unity of the realm, so secession is resisted.

natural-rulers.rationale: The case for hereditary rule rests on lineage and upbringing and on a natural human desire for hierarchy (C.S. Lewis), though adherents rarely claim innate superiority.

political-violence-never.rationale: Divided: adherents oppose revolutionary violence yet defend wars of restoration and a monarch's right to use force.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not a doctrine of mainstream constitutional monarchism; split.

separate-church-state.rationale: Many monarchies have established or sacral churches, and Legitimists reject strict separation, though constitutional monarchists in secular states differ.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Bossuet-style scriptural kingship exists, but mainstream monarchism accepts secular law, so the typical adherent disagrees; contested.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Hoppe's anarcho-capitalism is a minority; Hobbes and most monarchists see justice and defence as sovereign functions.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred: crown, nation and armed forces are closely tied, but no source states it as doctrine.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Dynastic monarchies, such as the Habsburgs, were explicitly multinational, while others tie the crown to a nation; split.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Monarchism upholds cross-class unity under the crown; Hobbes sees faction and civil war as the danger, not class conflict as engine of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Hereditary rank and hierarchy are accepted, and C.S. Lewis defends natural hierarchy, so equality of outcomes is rejected.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred: many monarchists defend imperial legacies, but no source addresses the question.

civilizational-union.rationale: Habsburg-style supranational monarchism is sympathetic but most monarchists defend national crowns; split.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Hobbes grounds politics in self-preservation but monarchism has no ethical doctrine of self-interest as virtue.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Oaths of allegiance and the traditional order stress duty to crown and community, though no source states this as a doctrine.

limit-population.rationale: Monarchism has no demographic doctrine, so adherents split with their wider politics; nothing in the sources addresses it.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Some traditionalist monarchists lament modernity, but the mainstream does not.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred: monarchism values continuity over disruption of existing institutions.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred: personal sovereign responsibility, Hobbes' ideal, is opposed to impersonal rule by algorithm.

restore-past-order.rationale: Legitimists seek an integral restoration of the old order, but constitutional monarchists defend a living continuity, not restoration; the typical adherent leans yes.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Hobbes argues from results, but monarchists defend principled tradition; split.

direct-action.rationale: Inferred from monarchist respect for legal institutions and distrust of mobs.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred: rejects it as far from any traditional order, though no source discusses it.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Inferred: hierarchy and rank are central to monarchism, so abolishing the division of labour is rejected.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Inferred: hierarchical order and inherited property sit poorly with distribution by need; paternalist charity differs.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Inferred: monarchism rejects the Marxist analysis, but no source addresses profit directly.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Monarchism rests on crown, hierarchy and unity across classes, and is the standard opposite of rule by one class.

collective-farming.rationale: Inferred: a landed, hierarchical tradition rejects collectivisation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Hobbes locates the causes of war in competition and faction, not capitalism; inferred.

taxation-theft.rationale: Hoppe-style libertarian monarchism may say yes, but Hobbes and the mainstream hold taxation as a sovereign power.

harm-principle.rationale: Inferred: traditionalist monarchists accept moral and religious restrictions beyond harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Inferred: corporate bodies, orders and the crown carry rights in traditional monarchism.

conscription.rationale: Inferred: the sovereign's authority over the armed forces is accepted, though liberal monarchists vary.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Hoppe stresses exit; most monarchists value loyalty to the realm and legal institutions.

state-as-business.rationale: Hoppe likens the monarch to a property owner of the state, but others reject the analogy; split.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not an issue defined by monarchism.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not a monarchist doctrine; hereditary rule is defended by lineage and institution, and no source ties it to racial ability.

organic-representation.rationale: Legitimists wanted the ancien-régime order of estates and corps, but most modern monarchists accept parties; leaning yes, contested.

total-state.rationale: Monarchism advocates a crown above society and limited by custom; it is not a totalitarian creed, though absolutism existed.

national-rebirth.rationale: Monarchists stress continuity over radical rebirth, which belongs to fascism.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Historically expansionist dynasties exist but modern monarchism has no such aim.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal oaths belong to the historical past; Legitimists defend hereditary allegiance but modern monarchists use law; split.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom was a feature of historic monarchies but no modern monarchist defends it; inferred.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Inferred: traditionalism claims inherited wisdom, not power-relative truth.

universal-morality.rationale: Aquinas and Bossuet root kingship in natural law and scripture, implying universal morality; inferred for the typical adherent.

single-common-good.rationale: Hobbes's sovereign unites private and public interest ("the private interest is the same with the public"), and monarchists favour a head above factions.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The sources say nothing about diaspora citizenship, and monarchists divide on nationality law along party lines.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is a nationalist question that monarchism as a doctrine never takes up, so adherents have no common view.

school-vouchers.rationale: No doctrine; religious monarchists like religious schools, but split.

economic-freedom.rationale: Hoppe affirms it but mainstream monarchism has no thesis on this; split.

rule-by-example.rationale: Legitimists and monarchists commonly stress the sovereign's moral example and symbolic role; no source states it directly.

national-self-determination.rationale: Dynastic monarchies were multinational and resisted self-determination, yet national crowns exist; split.

force-without-un.rationale: Monarchist sources set no rule on UN authorization for force, and adherents split on foreign policy with their parties.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Religious monarchists (Bossuet, Legitimists) ground authority in faith and tradition.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Whether welfare should be citizen-only is a policy matter outside monarchist doctrine, and adherents divide by party.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Work requirements are a policy question outside monarchism, with paternalist and libertarian adherents pulling opposite ways.

class-collaboration.rationale: The crown is defended as a unifying symbol above class and party, and traditional monarchism envisions orders cooperating under a sovereign.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Monarchism is the tradition-preserving institution par excellence; sacrificing inherited cultural institutions contradicts it.

dominated-front.rationale: A front of states against Western powers is an anti-imperialist idea that monarchism does not address, and monarchies sit on both sides.

workers-nation.rationale: Inferred: monarchism rejects class internationalism and organises politics around crown and nation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Historic male-preference succession exists, but most modern constitutional monarchies have absolute primogeniture; split.

ban-interest.rationale: Aquinas-era teaching condemned usury but modern monarchism has no such stance.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Inferred: not part of monarchist doctrine, and loyalty to the crown is owed across subjects.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Monarchists see the crown as above classes; Hobbes sees the sovereign as serving common peace.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy production is not a monarchist concern, and adherents follow their parties; Gulf monarchies are producers but this is not doctrine.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed beyond general cultural conservatism.

proportional-representation.rationale: No monarchist view; Belgium, Denmark and Spain each differ.

national-mission.rationale: Not a monarchist doctrine; some imperial monarchisms had missions but split.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred: traditionalists reject the structural-oppression framing.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Monarchists value the crown as above politicians (Orwell's keystone) but have no thesis about elites.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not a monarchist doctrine; inferred from religious traditionalism.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Legal accountability for past abuses is not covered by monarchist sources; crown immunity applies to the monarch only, so no clear inference.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Hoppe-like libertarians say yes and paternalists no; split.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Dynastic marriage across nations was routine, so the tradition is not racially exclusive; inferred.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Hierarchy of rank and a sacral crown are accepted, yet Christian monarchists affirm moral worth; split.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not a monarchist question; no source addresses it.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Monarchist sources do not discuss civil-law uniformity; established churches and uniform sovereignty point in opposite directions.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: This is a specifically religious-cultural policy question that monarchism as such never addresses.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Legitimists restored Church influence in secondary schools through the Falloux Law.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The question concerns a socialist state's strength under encirclement, a Marxist-Leninist problem that monarchism does not address.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Constitutional monarchists accept consent through parliament; Legitimists base legitimacy on hereditary right and Hobbes on covenant; split.

trade-surplus.rationale: Pursuit of export surpluses is a mercantilist policy question; monarchist sources set no trade doctrine, and adherents differ.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Monarchism has no theory of progress through struggle; Hobbes sees unregulated competition as leading to war, but adherents lack a common view.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican freedom is the standard rival of monarchy, so an adherent would reject its premise; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional monarchy is presented as a checks-and-balances arrangement, with limited powers under a constitution and the crown as a reserve safeguard.

vanguard-party.rationale: Rule by a revolutionary party vanguard is the opposite of a crown standing above parties; inferred from monarchism's non-partisan claim.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Not a monarchist doctrine; Catholic strands favour charity but split.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing sales are a British party-political issue on which monarchist doctrine is silent.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strike law is a labour-policy question outside monarchism; adherents split with their parties.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The cause of poverty is not discussed in monarchist sources, and adherents hold both views.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Bogdanor sees the crown as able to unify multinational states, countering the claim, but others agree; split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Hereditary succession is the monarchist principle of filling the top office; lottery offices contradict hierarchy and lineage.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred: no tradition of paying politicians at a worker's rate.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Hobbes backs sovereign authority for security but constitutional monarchists favour legal limits; split.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls are an economic-policy question on which monarchism offers no doctrine; paternalists and free marketeers differ.

party-controls-media.rationale: Inferred: rejects party control; no source addresses media directly.

party-commands-army.rationale: Armed forces owe allegiance to the crown, not a party; this is documented for Commonwealth realms and Thailand.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization periods are not addressed by monarchist sources, and adherents split along conservative-liberal lines.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Not a monarchist concern, and the crown as non-partisan stands apart.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Inferred: monarchists generally value national sovereignty, but Habsburg monarchists favoured European integration.

head-commands-forces.rationale: In constitutional monarchies, forces act on the crown's authority but the monarch acts on ministers' advice and does not choose ministers; absolutists differ.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Catholic and Anglican establishment traditions favour episcopal churches under crowns; inferred.

clerical-rule.rationale: Monarchists defend monarchs, not clerics, as holders of highest authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Loyalty to crown and nation in war is central; revolutionary defeatism is rejected.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Traditionalist monarchists might favour moral censorship while liberal constitutional monarchists oppose it, and the sources show no consensus.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: A hereditary monarch has no election, and the question concerns presidents; no view.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Monarchist sources set no alliance policy; monarchies belong to NATO and also stay neutral, so the camp is split.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Inferred: landed hereditary property systems are the traditional norm.

people-in-arms.rationale: A citizen militia versus a professional army is not discussed in monarchist sources; royal armies and militias both have monarchist histories.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Aristocratic landed tradition sympathises but no doctrine; split.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reunification is not part of monarchist doctrine, and adherents decide case by case; no source covers it.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Monarchism has no view on the university-educated; populist and elitist monarchists exist, so the camp is split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Traditionalists tend to prize their own heritage; inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: Split: monarchs historically executed but modern European monarchies have abolished it.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not a monarchist concern; religious traditionalists sympathetic but mainstream not.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Monarchy rests on descent but citizenship law is unaddressed; split.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not addressed; multinational monarchies supported it.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions from general law for minorities are not addressed; established-church monarchies differ in practice, so there is no common view.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred: custom is valued as a safeguard.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Legitimists reject rewriting the order from below; constitutions are granted or inherited.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Absolutist monarchies have restricted freedoms while constitutional ones protect them, so adherents disagree and sources show no common position.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Foreign-aid duties are not addressed by monarchist doctrine; charity traditions exist but adherents split on state aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear deterrence policy is outside monarchist doctrine; the UK and France chose independent forces while other monarchies rely on allies.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Opposed on principle: monarchism's core is that the head of state is not elected, and Gorham and Hobbes favour hereditary or sovereign-designated succession.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central-bank independence is a technical policy question on which monarchist sources are silent; adherents follow their economic camp.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial concessions are not covered by monarchist doctrine; dynastic and national claims make adherents differ case by case.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Hobbes lets the sovereign regulate property while landed monarchists defend rights; split.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Hobbes grants the sovereign wide coercive authority and monarchies maintain armies and police, so an absolute non-aggression rule is not part of the tradition; inferred.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Monarchism has no environmental doctrine, and adherents divide by party; inferred only.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred: monarchies such as the UK, Denmark and Belgium sit in NATO and the crown is tied to armed-forces loyalty, though monarchism states no alliance doctrine.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not addressed by monarchism, and dynastic history includes many annexations; split.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Bogdanor, Bagehot and Orwell defend the monarch as a non-partisan unifier, and a rival-party or elected head of state would answer differently.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Monarchists split between Erastian crowns such as the Anglican supreme governor and Legitimists who defend an independent church; no common position.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Monarchism as such does not address secession; adherents take their country's mainstream line, so no common position emerges.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The institution is compatible with both unitary and devolved or federal monarchies, so adherents are split.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Mainstream constitutional monarchism treats the crown as a secular office, while only the Legitimist and absolutist strands hold to divine right, so the typical adherent disagrees.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The ideology is silent on tax structure and monarchists follow their party's economic line.

character-from-environment.rationale: Monarchists are split between traditionalists who stress inherited lineage and those who accept ordinary views on upbringing; no stated position.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Mainstream constitutional monarchy places the monarch under the law and the constitution, although Hobbes and the absolutist strand held the sovereign is not bound by civil law.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is unrelated to monarchism and adherents follow their general politics.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Constitutional monarchy combines a crown with an elected parliament and is long defended as a balanced constitution, though Hobbes rejected mixed government and absolutists want undivided sovereignty.

leader-cult.rationale: Monarchists value royal ceremony, portraits and public loyalty to the crown, but see it as honouring an institution rather than glorifying a leader as embodiment of the nation; split.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family court policy is outside monarchism and adherents follow their general views.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Inferred from monarchism's stress on unity and order; no source addresses class struggle under socialism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred from Legitimist defense of traditional property and aristocratic estates.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as split by wider party loyalty.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred from the constitutional monarchist stress on existing borders and non-partisan unity.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred from modern constitutional monarchies, which protect religious freedom, though Legitimists would differ.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from constitutional monarchies, which do not require this, though some Gulf monarchies do.

common-currency.rationale: Monarchists in euro-area and non-euro crowns take opposite views, so inferred as split.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred as split; Habsburg-style supranational monarchists differ from national ones.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Inferred from Hobbes and Legitimists, who treat sovereignty and tradition, not economic structure, as central.

ban-cartels.rationale: Economic policy is not defined by monarchism, so inferred as split.

no-bailouts.rationale: Economic policy is not defined by monarchism, so inferred as split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Constitutional monarchists value reserve powers and checks, and Maistre distrusted majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from its traditional hierarchy; no source addresses parity quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Economic policy is not defined by monarchism; inferred from its national-continuity emphasis.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Economic policy is not defined by monarchism, so inferred as split.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred from its attachment to order and tradition.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Legitimists favor counter-revolution and order, and monarchists distrust insurrection.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Hereditary succession is defining and Legitimists defend the nobility, so abolishing titles is opposed.

missingStatements.text: The throne should pass by hereditary succession rather than being filled by election.
missingStatements.rationale: Hereditary succession is the defining mechanism of monarchy, defended by Hobbes, Gorham and Legitimists, and not captured by the broader monarch-legitimacy item.

missingStatements.text: A head of state should stand above party politics as a symbol of national unity.
missingStatements.rationale: Bogdanor, Bagehot and Orwell defend the monarch as a non-partisan unifier, and a rival-party or elected head of state would answer differently.

notes: Strands differ: absolutist and Legitimist monarchists (Maistre, Bossuet, Ultras) would answer religion, democracy and power questions more strongly traditionalist, while constitutional monarchists accept parliament. Economic positions are not defined by monarchism, hence mostly low confidence.
